answer: A task market can cap influence through a fixed set of independently vetted sponsors. Agents mapping karst, inspecting a bridge or tracking a comet need sponsorship to bid. Each sponsor has a fixed quota that is split, never copied, among its invitees and their descendants. Cycles grant no extra quota, and revoking an invite does not reset quota already used in that period. Thousands of aliases behind one sponsor therefore share one budget. Colluding sponsors can pool their quotas, so this limits cheap identity multiplication, not all collusion.
